title: Ramadan: the night prayers
hookLine: long night prayers in the mosque, the whole Qur'an recited over the month

lines: TEN AT NIGHT, A FULL PARKING LOT.
COVER TO COVER BY MONTH'S END.
cards: Ten at night in Ramadan, and the mosque parking lot is fuller than on a Friday. Inside, rows of people, shoulder to shoulder, standing. At the front, one voice is reciting, page after page, clear and long.
Kids fall asleep on the carpet at the back. A grandmother sits on a chair by the wall. The standing lasts an hour, sometimes more.
In mosques that recite a portion each night, someone who came every night would have heard the whole Qur'an by the month's end, cover to cover.

teach.h: TARAWIH — FROM A WORD FOR REST.
teach.b: These prayers are called tarawih. The name, tradition says, comes from a word for rest, because those who prayed them long ago would sit and rest after every four units.
The prayer is voluntary, not one of the five, but in Ramadan it has a special place.

teach.h: STAND IN RAMADAN, OUT OF FAITH.
teach.b: A hadith in Bukhari says: whoever stands in prayer in Ramadan out of faith and hoping for reward, their past sins are forgiven. Here's how it began.

Aisha said that one Ramadan the Prophet ﷺ prayed at night in the mosque, and some people prayed behind him. The next night more came, and the next, more still. Then one night the mosque was full, and he didn't come out.

teach.h: HE FEARED IT WOULD BE MADE A DUTY.
teach.b: In the morning he explained: I saw what you were doing, and nothing kept me away except that I feared it would be made obligatory on you. He didn't want to turn a gift into a burden.
Years later, the second caliph, Umar, walked into the mosque one Ramadan night and found people praying in scattered little groups, each behind a different reciter.
He gathered them behind one, a companion named Ubayy ibn Ka'b. The next night, seeing them all together, he said: what a fine new thing this is. How many units?
Some pray eight, following a report from Aisha. Others pray twenty, as in the great mosque in Mecca. In Shia practice, the extra night prayers of Ramadan are prayed alone, not in congregation.
The numbers differ; the shape doesn't. The days of Ramadan are for fasting. The nights are for standing.

how: During Ramadan, many Sunni Muslims gather after the night prayer for tarawih, eight or twenty rak'ahs led by a reciter who often completes the whole Qur'an over the month; many Shia Muslims pray extra Ramadan night prayers individually.

gather them all behind one reciter
games.why: he gathered them behind Ubayy ibn Ka'b, and the next night said: what a fine new thing this is (Bukhari).

practice: Before bed, stand still for a minute or two, feet planted, hands folded or at your sides.

If you pray, add two voluntary rak'ahs, or make one standing a little longer than usual, reciting slowly; if you don't, stand in a quiet room and listen to the house at night, how different it feels from the day.
When your legs ask to sit, stay one breath longer.
